html:
The Resígaro are a tiny Indigenous people of Loreto in the Peruvian Amazon, living in the northeast of the region among the Bora and Ocaina peoples. Their language is Arawakan, part of the Arawakan family, though it borrowed much from its neighbours.

They were nearly destroyed in the Putumayo genocide of the early 1900s, when the rubber company of Julio César Arana enslaved and killed thousands of people across the region during the rubber boom. The few survivors married into Bora and Ocaina families. By the 2010s only one or two speakers of Resígaro were left, and the language is close to extinct. They live today in Peru.
